questions.q: Which actor already has legitimate access to the environment?
questions.explain: An insider is an authorized user: perimeter controls do not block them.

questions.q: A ransomware campaign demanding payment primarily falls under which motivation?
questions.explain: Financial gain and extortion characterize organized crime, even if the tool can be reused by other actors.

questions.q: Match each actor to their most typical motivation.
questions.explain: Motivation is the reliable classification criterion, regardless of the tool used.

questions.q: Which attributes are used to characterize a threat actor? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: These are the three official attributes in objective 2.2.

options: Attribute based on a single IP address
Attribute based on a body of evidence, with a confidence level
Refuse any attribution, even with evidence
questions.explain: Tools and infrastructure are shared: attribution is probabilistic and must be reassessed.

questions.q: A user clicks a phishing link with no intent to cause harm. Which actor best describes this profile?
questions.explain: The lack of intent qualifies an accidental actor, even if their action opens the door to another threat actor.
